country.comment: Examines 53 municipalities in the Colombian departments of Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda.
country.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 6, Catastro y SGP; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos (Figura 1)

effect_estimate.comment: Cadastral updating in isolation did not consistently increase property tax revenues, SGP water/sanitation transfers, aqueduct coverage, or drinking water quality; statistically significant post-update increases were concentrated in sewerage subscribers and sewerage coverage (66.67% of analyzed municipalities).
effect_estimate.value: In municipality-by-municipality robust paired-samples t-tests (alpha = 0.05) comparing 5 years before vs. 5 years after cadastral updating: (1) Aqueduct subscribers increased significantly in 8 of 33 municipalities (24.24%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.77; no significant difference in 75.76%), and proxy aqueduct coverage (subscribers/parcels) increased significantly in 5 of 33 municipalities (15.15%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.82; no significant difference in 84.85%); (2) Sewerage subscribers increased significantly in 22 of 33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56; no significant difference in 33.33%), and proxy sewerage coverage increased significantly in 22 of 33 municipalities (66.67%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.56; no significant difference in 33.33%); (3) Water Quality Risk Index (IRCA) increased significantly (higher risk) in 12 of 42 municipalities (28.57%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.87; no significant difference in 71.43%); (4) Property tax revenue increased significantly in 27 of 53 municipalities (50.94%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.80), per capita property tax revenue increased significantly in 29 of 53 municipalities (54.72%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.69), and SGP drinking water and basic sanitation transfers increased significantly in 13 of 52 municipalities (25.00%, p < 0.05, Cohen's d > 0.81).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 9-16, Resultados and Tablas 2-7; PDF p. 17, Conclusiones

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented association): the study documents pre-post statistical differences in municipal fiscal and water/sanitation indicators following cadastral updates, but carries Serious/Critical confounding risk from secular time trends and concurrent municipal reforms (precluding level 3) and does not directly observe the internal administrative mechanisms linking cadastral updating to household connections or infrastructure investment (as noted in the Limitations on PDF p. 17).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 6-7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 11 & p. 16-17, Resultados and Conclusiones

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines municipal cadastral updating, parcel registration/valuation, and property taxation (property), use of cadastre and coverage certification for municipal infrastructure planning and multipurpose policy formulation (planning), and central-local intergovernmental fiscal transfers and agency coordination across DNP/SGP, IGAC, SSPD, and municipalities (political_coordination).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 5-6, Impuesto Predial and Catastro y SGP; PDF p. 11, Resultados; PDF p. 17, Conclusiones

outcome_flags.comment: Measures formal aqueduct and sewerage utility subscribers reported to SUI (formal_connection, water_access, sanitation_access), proxy aqueduct and sewerage coverage per cadastral parcel (service_coverage), and drinking water quality via the IRCA Water Quality Risk Index (service_quality).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF p. 4, Introducción; PDF p. 6-7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 13-16, Tablas 5-7

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Appraised with ROBINS-I because the study explicitly evaluates the impact of a non-randomized municipal administrative intervention (cadastral updating) using longitudinal pre-intervention vs. post-intervention comparisons (two 5-year windows per municipality). Because it relies on uncontrolled within-municipality paired t-tests without an untreated control group or adjustment for secular trends and concurrent fiscal policies, overall ROBINS-I risk of bias is Serious/Critical.
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 6-7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1

sample_size.comment: Each municipality is observed across two 5-year periods before and after its cadastral update year (10 years per municipality within 2000-2020; 4-year windows in some utility series due to missing data). Note that Tables 2-4 print partial row subsets on PDF pp. 9-10 and 12 while the Results text explicitly reports analyses on 53 and 52 municipalities, respectively.
sample_size.value: 53 municipalities across 3 departments (Caldas, Quindío, and Risaralda) observed over two 5-year periods (analytical subsamples: n = 53 municipalities for property tax and per capita property tax; n = 52 municipalities for SGP water and basic sanitation transfers; n = 33 municipalities for aqueduct and sewerage subscribers and coverage; n = 42 municipalities for IRCA water quality)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1; PDF p. 11 & p. 16, Resultados

study_design.comment: Quantitative pre-post municipal panel analysis comparing 5 annual observations before vs. 5 annual observations after each municipality's cadastral update (staggered 2004-2015) using the Yuen-Wilcox Robust Paired Samples T-Test in JAMOVI (Walrus library), without an untreated comparator group or multivariable regression controls.
study_design.value: Longitudinal pre-post observational municipal study using robust paired-samples t-tests (two 5-year periods before and after cadastral updating)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Resumen; PDF p. 6-7, Metodología y Datos; PDF p. 8, Tabla 1
